rule: Call on a receiver of **unknown type**: `recv.member`, using the LAST receiver segment (`self.client.get()` → `client.get`; `a.b.c()` → `b.c`). Call on a **computed receiver** (call result, index, literal, `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member` — a leading dot means "receiver unknown". **low**: a guess — receiver of unknown type (`recv.m`, `.m`), or a bare name not found in the scan.
notes: Parameters of unknown type -> `recv.m`, low. A call result (`opts.fetch(:a)`, `conn.pool()`), a string literal and an array literal are computed receivers -> `.m`, low. In Ruby `conn.pool()` is a method call, so `.checkout` is on a call result (not `pool.checkout`). `f = Fetcher.new; f.run()` stays `f.run`, low: decision A applies to statically typed languages and typed PHP/Groovy declarations only. Symbol `:a` is not a call.
